review_notes: I read the whole target file, and the relevant parts of the RelativeGroupLaw definition file. The two findings below come from comparing proof blocks inside `main` and the pullback-lift API. I did not report the repeated "Spec of a field has one point, so its ideal is ⊥" snippets (lines 155-158, 165, 307, 311-313, 332) because each is only a few lines. I also did not report the `torsLift`/`liftPt` definitions as near-duplicates, since that is an API-duplication issue rather than repeated proof reasoning. I could not compile anything, so the proposed lemma statements and proof sketches are untested. They are written against the hypotheses actually available at each use.

findings.declaration: GoodReductionJacobian.LevelL3.main (hγeq in the two directions of hset)
findings.excerpt: have hγeq : γ = γ ≫ L.schemeKerStr n ≫ τ c := by
findings.problem: The two halves of `hset` each redo the same pullback argument. A map γ into `L.schemeKer n` equals `t ≫ τ c` exactly when its first projection equals `t ≫ (σ c).1`, given γ ≫ schemeKerStr = t. The forward half (lines 318-326) proves this by `pullback.hom_ext`, using `hτfst` for the fst component and `hτ` for the snd component. The reverse half (lines 347-357) applies `fst` to `hγeq` and then runs a long chain of `Category.assoc` rewrites, `change`/`show` and `liftPt_snd` to obtain the fst equality. The same `torsLift` fst/snd bookkeeping is therefore written twice, in opposite directions, with fragile `change`/`show` steps.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma next to `torsLift`:
`theorem eq_comp_torsLift_iff (n) (σ : SchemeHomOver (𝟙 _) f) (hσ : L.nsmul (𝟙 _) n σ = L.one (𝟙 _)) {T} (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of S)) (γ : T ⟶ L.schemeKer n) (hγ : γ ≫ L.schemeKerStr n = t) : γ = t ≫ torsLift L n σ hσ ↔ γ ≫ pullback.fst _ _ = t ≫ σ.1`.
Proof sketch: (→) rewrite with the equation, then `Category.assoc` and `torsLift_fst`. (←) `pullback.hom_ext`. The fst component is `Category.assoc, torsLift_fst, ← h`. The snd component is `Category.assoc, torsLift_snd, Category.comp_id, hγ`.
Forward use: with t := Spec.map (ofHom sk), `hγ := hsk.symm` and `h3 : Spec.map (ofHom sk) ≫ (σ c).1 = γ ≫ pullback.fst _ _` (already derived at line 321), `hγeq` becomes `(eq_comp_torsLift_iff L n (σ c) (hσ c) _ γ hsk.symm).mpr h3.symm`. `hdictV` then needs the `t ≫ τ c` form, or a rewrite with `hsk.symm`.
Reverse use: with t := Spec.map (ofHom sk) and `hγ := liftPt_snd L n _ Q hQ`, the lemma gives `γ ≫ fst = Spec.map (ofHom sk) ≫ (σ c).1` from `hγeq`. The goal is then `by rw [← liftPt_fst L n _ Q hQ]; exact this.symm`, which replaces lines 353-357. Both uses stay within the existing hypotheses and imports.
findings.benefit: The pullback comparison is proved once, as a named statement, instead of as two inverse ad-hoc computations. The final steps of `main` shrink to one-line applications. The `change`/`show` rewrites that depend on the exact elaborated form of `τ c` and `liftPt` disappear.

findings.problem: Three proofs each re-derive that the identity section over t is the pullback of the identity section over the base: `(L.one t).1 = (L.one (𝟙 _)).1 ≫ t`. Each time they apply `← L.one_natural (𝟙 _) t t (Category.comp_id _)` and then `schemeHomOverComp_coe`. This happens in `htors` (lines 135-138), in `kerPt_torsion` (lines 194-195) and in the side proof of `liftPt` (line 200). The pattern is fiddly because the unification of `(𝟙 _)` and `Category.comp_id _` is repeated and the result passes through `schemeHomOverComp`. It is also the one step whose rewrite direction has to be chosen carefully in each of the three places.
findings.proposed_change:
Add a lemma before `isFinite_etale_schemeKerStr`:
`theorem one_coe_eq_comp {T} (t : T ⟶ Spec (CommRingCat.of S)) : (L.one t).1 = (L.one (𝟙 (Spec (CommRingCat.of S)))).1 ≫ t := by have h := L.one_natural (𝟙 _) t t (Category.comp_id _); exact (congrArg Subtype.val h).symm` (the `schemeHomOverComp_coe` rewrite goes inside this proof).
Then `kerPt_torsion` ends with `rw [Category.assoc, pullback.condition, ← Category.assoc, hγ, one_coe_eq_comp]`. The proof of `liftPt` becomes `by rw [comp_schemeNsmul, hQ, one_coe_eq_comp]`. In `htors`, the proof of `hP` becomes `Subtype.ext (by rw [one_coe_eq_comp, ← hP₀, ht])`.
The hypotheses are the same, since `t` is arbitrary in all three places.
findings.benefit: The relation between `L.one t` and `L.one (𝟙 _)` is recorded once under a readable name. The three sites stop repeating the unification-sensitive `one_natural` rewrite. A future change to how `one` is pulled back needs one edit instead of three.
